### § 1. Office of Inspector General:  Office Established. {#s-1}

```{=html}
<p>There is an Office of the Inspector General, the head of which is the Inspector General.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 18-008, ratified Nov. 6, 2018</p>
```


### § 2. Office of Inspector General: Advisory board. {#s-2}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Inspector General is appointed by an advisory board to be comprised of 11members as provided in <a href="article-x.html#s-2">this section</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The advisory board is entitle to the assistance of the Baltimore City Department of Human Resources for purposes of advertising a vacancy and interviewing and hiring candidates for the position of Inspector General.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>The Mayor must provide the advisory board with access to City resources to facilitate the advisory board’s completion of its responsibilities.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Qualifications.</span></p>
<p>An individual is qualified to serve as a member of the advisory board if the individual:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>is a Baltimore City resident;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>is over the age of 21 years old;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>has never been convicted of an offense under Section 16-201(a)(5) or (6) of the State Election Law Article; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>has a background in, or familiarity with, ethics, law, program or performance evaluation, or accounting or has a familiarity with the Office of the Inspector General and the duties of the Office.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Eligibility.</span></p>
<p>In addition to the required qualifications in <a href="article-x.html#s-2">subsection (b) of this section</a>, an applicant is not eligible for appointment to the advisory board if the individual:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>is or becomes an employee or elected officer of:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>the State of Maryland;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>the City of Baltimore;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>any State or City agency, instrumentality, or any other unit of a State entity except:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">(A)</span></p>
<p>a State college;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">(B)</span></p>
<p>a State university; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">(C)</span></p>
<p>another institution of higher education;</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>is or becomes a candidate for elected public office of:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>the State of Maryland;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>the City of Baltimore; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>any county or municipality of the State.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>is or becomes an elected municipal officer's:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>spouse;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>parent;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>child; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iv)</span></p>
<p>sibling;</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>is or becomes a responsible officer, as defined in Section 1-101(mm) of the State Election Law Article;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>is or becomes employed by the City of Baltimore or the State of Maryland in any capacity;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<p>is or becomes a lobbyist under:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>the State General Provisions Article, Title 5 {“Maryland Public Ethics Law”};</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>Article 8, Subtitle 8 {“Lobbying”} of the City Code; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>the ethics code of any political subdivision of the State; or</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(7)</span></p>
<p>is or becomes associated with a business entity as described in Article 8, Section 6-6 {“Prohibited participation”} of the City Code.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Nomination process: In general.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>An individual who meets the requirements set forth in subsections (b) and (c) of <a href="article-x.html#s-2">this section</a> may submit an application to the member of the City Council who represents the district in which the individual resides, in the form required by the Board of Ethics.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>Each member of the City Council must:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>review the applications received pursuant to paragraph (1) of this subsection; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>select 1 applicant as the nominee to the advisory board from that member's district.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Nomination process: Diversity.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The membership of the advisory board must be inclusive and reflect the racial and gender diversity of the City of Baltimore.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>A member of the City Council must give reasonable consideration to the diversity of the member's district when selecting a nominee to the advisory board.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Nomination process: Final appointments.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>Final random selections to the advisory board must be made by the Chair of the Board of Ethics, pursuant to <a href="article-vii.html#s-110">Article VII, Section 110</a> of this Charter.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>7 of the 11 members of the advisory board must be randomly selected by the Chair of the Board of Ethics on the following basis:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>1 member from among the 2 nominees submitted from City Council districts 1 and 2;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>1 member from among the 2 nominees submitted from City Council districts 3 and 4;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>1 member from among the 2 nominees submitted from City Council districts 5 and 6;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iv)</span></p>
<p>1 member from among the 2 nominees submitted from City Council districts 7 and 8;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(v)</span></p>
<p>1 member from among the 2 nominees submitted from City Council districts 9 and 10;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(vi)</span></p>
<p>1 member from among the 2 nominees submitted from City Council Districts 11 and 12; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(vii)</span></p>
<p>1 member from among the 2 nominees submitted from City Council districts 13 and 14.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>The remaining 4 members shall consist of:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>1 member of the Association of Certified Fraud Examiners, selected by the Board of Regents of the Association of Certified Fraud Examiners;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>1 member of the Maryland Association of Certified Public Accountants, selected by the Board of Directors of the Maryland Association of Certified Public Accountants;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>the Dean of the University of Maryland School of Law or the Dean’s designee; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iv)</span></p>
<p>the Dean of the University of Baltimore School of Law, or the Dean’s designee.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>The 4 members of the advisory board selected pursuant to  paragraph (3) of this subsection must also comply with all eligibility and qualification requirements for advisory board members outlined in this subsection.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(g)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Term of members.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The terms of the members of the advisory board must be staggered and may not be coterminous with the Mayor’s term of office.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>Of the initial 11 appointments to the advisory board:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>the members appointed pursuant to paragraphs (2)(v) and (3) of <a href="article-x.html#s-2">Subsection (f) of this section</a> must each serve a term of 3 years; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>the remaining members must each serve a term of 4 years.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>After the initial terms of the advisory board members have expired, a member of the advisory board shall serve a term of 4 years.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>The term required by paragraph (2)(i) of this subsection shall be considered a full term for the purposes of the term limits established in <a href="article-iv.html#s-6">Article IV, Section 6(e)</a> of this Charter.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>No member of the advisory board may serve more than 2 consecutive full terms.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(h)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Removal of advisory board member.</span></p>
<p>A member of the advisory board may be removed for cause by a vote of the majority of the members of the advisory board.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Vacancies.</span></p>
<p>The Chair of the Board of Ethics shall select at random a member from the nominations submitted at the outset of that particular position's term.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(j)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Procedures.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>A quorum of the advisory board consists of 6 members.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The advisory board shall elect a chair from the membership of the advisory board.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>An affirmative vote of at least 6 members shall be necessary to appoint an Inspector General.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(k)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Required training.</span></p>
<p>Prior to beginning their duties, the members of the advisory board shall attend a training session, to be provided by the Office of the Inspector General, that details:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>the rules governing the advisory board; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>the rules governing and duties of the Inspector General.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(l)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Annual overview.</span></p>
<p>The advisory board shall appear before the City Council at least once a year to provide the City Council with an overview of the activities of the advisory board and the Office of the Inspector General.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```


### § 3. Office of Inspector General:  The Inspector General. {#s-3}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Qualifications.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Inspector General shall be appointed without regard to political affiliation and must have substantial experience in auditing, financial analysis, criminal justice law, management analysis, public administration, investigations, or another appropriate field.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The Inspector General shall hold at the time of appointment, or be required to obtain within 7 months after appointment, certification as a Certified Inspector General.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Term.</span></p>
<p>The Inspector General shall serve a term of 6 years commencing from the date of appointment.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Removal.</span></p>
<p>The Inspector General may be removed from office by an affirmative vote of a majority of the members of the advisory board for:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>misconduct in office;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>persistent failure to perform the duties of office; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>conduct prejudicial to the proper administration of justice.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Reports concerning a vacancy or incapacity.</span></p>
<p>Whenever the Office of the Inspector general remains vacant for 180 days, or whenever the Inspector General is incapacitated or otherwise unable to perform the duties of the office for 180 days, the Chair of the advisory board shall issue a report to the City Council on the 180th day, and every 2 months thereafter until the vacancy is filled or the Inspector General reports to work, describing the status of the efforts to fill the vacancy or the status of the Absent Inspector General.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Performance review.</span></p>
<p>The advisory board shall meet at least once annually to review the performance of the Inspector General.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 18-008, ratified Nov. 6, 2018; Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```


### § 4. Office of Inspector General:  Powers and Duties. {#s-4}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">IG as head of Office.</span></p>
<p>The Inspector General shall supervise and direct the Office of the Inspector General.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Responsibilities of Office.</span></p>
<p>The Office of the Inspector General is responsible for:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>investigating complaints of fraud, financial waste, and abuse in City government; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>promoting efficiency, accountability, and integrity in City government.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Jurisdiction of Office.</span></p>
<p>The Office of the Inspector General may investigate allegations that involve City government and potential violations of laws or regulations by any:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>City elected official;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>City employee;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>member of a board or commission established or governed by the City Charter, City Code, or an executive order issued by the Mayor;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>City contractor or person negotiating a contract with the City;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>person seeking certification to provide goods or services to the City; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<p>external recipient of City funds, benefits, or services.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Issuing subpoenas.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>To perform the duties of office, the Inspector General may issue a subpoena to require:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>any person to appear under oath as a witness; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>the production of any information, document, report, record, account, or other material.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The Inspector General may enforce any subpoena issued pursuant to this subsection in any court of competent jurisdiction.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Annual report.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Office of the Inspector General shall prepare and publish an annual report of the Office’s activities.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The annual report may include recommendations regarding program weakness, contracting irregularities, or other institutional problems discovered by the Office.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>The annual report shall be:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>submitted to all of the members of the advisory board; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>after any redactions required by law, posted on the Office of the Inspector General’s website.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 18-008, ratified Nov. 6, 2018; Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```


### § 5. Office of Inspector General:  Budget. {#s-5}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">IG to prepare proposed budget.</span></p>
<p>The Inspector General shall formulate and prepare annually, or as frequently as required by law, a proposed budget to fund the operations of the Office and shall transmit the proposed budget to the advisory board for its review.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Advisory board to approve or revise.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The advisory board shall meet to review the proposed budget submitted by the Inspector General for the purpose of assessing and determining whether, in the judgement of the advisory board, the proposed budget provides sufficient funding to meet the duties of the Office.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The advisory board shall, by an affirmative vote of at least 4 of its members, either:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>approve the proposed budget as submitted; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>revise the proposed budget if the advisory board disagrees with the substance of any item contained in the proposed budget, including estimates of need and amounts of requested funding.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Submission.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The budget approved by the advisory board pursuant to <a href="article-x.html#s-5">subsection (b) of this section</a> shall be the Office budget the advisory board recommends to the Board of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The advisory board, on behalf of the Office of the Inspector General, shall submit the recommended budget to the Board of Estimates in a timely manner in order for the recommended budget to be considered for inclusion in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Funding.</span></p>
<p>The Office of the Inspector General shall be funded annually in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 18-008, ratified Nov. 6, 2018; Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```


### § 6. Office of Inspector General:  Administration and Operation. {#s-6}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Staff.</span></p>
<p>The Inspector General may appoint such other employees to assist in the conduct of the Office as may be provided in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Deputy Inspector General.</span></p>
<p>The Inspector General shall appoint a Deputy Inspector General, who shall serve as the Acting Inspector General if the Inspector General is absent or unavailable for duty.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Administrative and operational procedures.</span></p>
<p>The administrative and operational procedures of the Office may be established by law or by rule or regulation adopted by the Inspector General.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 18-008, ratified Nov. 6, 2018; Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```


### § 7. Office of Inspector General:  Transition Provisions. {#s-7}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Incumbent Inspector General.</span></p>
<p>The individual holding the position of Inspector General of the City of Baltimore in the Law Department on November 6, 2018, will assume the position of Inspector General created by <a href="article-x.html">this Article</a> on the date <a href="article-x.html">this Article</a> goes into effect.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Initial term .</span></p>
<p>The 6 year term of the Inspector General who assumes office under the provisions of <a href="article-x.html">this Article</a> runs from the effective date of <a href="article-x.html">this Article</a>.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 18-008, ratified Nov. 6, 2018; Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```
